text:
maria: heads-up — CI microbench failure on PR #18450. Kernel-selector hotloop test exceeds threshold: median latency +12% (was 42ms -> 47ms). Failing test: runtime/kernel_selector::hotloop_switch_benchmark

dev-ci-bot: [alert] ci/perf-microbench failed for PR 18450
Artifacts: https://ci.redwood.internal/artifacts/18450/bench-logs.tar.gz
Golden: s3://redwood-ci/goldens/kernel-selector/2026-03-18

alex: ugh. did this come from the quant-kernel change merged yesterday? PR 18390

lin: grabbing logs
lin: quick snippet from flamegraph: spike in kernel_dispatch (~0x7f3e...) at warmup path, heavy in autoselect path

kevin: also seeing increased minor page-faults in warmup on the perf traces. running local bisect now

sara: assigning to @kevin and @lin — if it's a regress we should block the rollout and stop Dedicated canary

kevin: bisect update: commit 7a3f2e4 (runtime/autoselect: prefer quantized concat for shortseq) reproduces the +11-12% locally. stepping through next

maria: that commit changed kernel priority ordering; plausible it forces a slower kernel for mixed-quant models. can you run microbench with --force-kernel=legacy to confirm?

kevin: ran with --force-kernel=legacy -> latency back to baseline. with autoselect -> +11.8% (repro). confirmed regression linked to autoselect choice.

alex: options: 1) tweak autoselect cost table to prefer legacy for <128 tokens, 2) add hysteresis to avoid flapping, 3) revert the quant-pref change.

lin: submitted quick patch PR 18457: autoselect: add hysteresis + pre-warm preference for legacy on shortseq. queued perf runs.

dev-ci-bot: perf job queued for PR 18457: https://ci.redwood.internal/builds/18457/perf (artifact will appear in ~10m)

sara: if 18457 passes we can hotfix and unblock rollout, otherwise revert 7a3f2e4. this is a rollout blocker for Dedicated.

ryan: +1 on revert if hotfix doesn't land in 2h. we can't risk Dedicated SLA customers with a perf regression.

kevin: perf results for 18457 (initial): median delta +1.2% vs baseline, tail unchanged. noise threshold is 2% so this is within acceptable.

maria: good signal. would still like to drive it under 0.5% in follow-up, but merging this to stop the blocker seems reasonable.

sara: merging 18457 now and kicking canary on 3 hosts. will monitor metrics.

dev-deploy-bot: canary rollout started: canary-group=kernel-selector-patch on fleet-3

alex: watching dashboards — tail p99 looks stable so far, no spike in page-faults. :thumbsup:

maria: created follow-up issue to add a unit/integration perf test for kernel_autoselect cost-model (RED-3891): https://issues.redwood/internal/RED-3891

kevin: adding flamegraphs and perf traces to PR for postmortem. attaching artifacts to the issue.

maria: thanks everyone. if anything spikes in canary we revert immediately and reopen the thread. closing for now.
